name: Lakshmi Mittal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Lakshmi Mittal is executive chairman of $61.3 billion (revenue) ArcelorMittal, the world's largest steel and mining company by output. His son, Aditya, is CEO since 2021.
Hailing from a steel clan, he separated from his siblings to start Mittal Steel then went on to merge the company with France's Arcelor in 2006.
ArcelorMittal reported net income of $3.15 billion in 2025, a 142% rise from $1.3 billion in 2024.
A long-time resident of the U.K., Mittal shifted his base to Switzerland following an exodus of the wealthy hit by the U.K.'s new tax regime.
In May 2026, he agreed to buy Indian Premier League cricket team Rajasthan Royals for $1.65 billion together with Adar Poonawalla, the son of vaccine billionaire Cyrus Poonawalla.
forbes_facts: In 2019, Arcelor and Nippon Steel completed their $5.9 billion acquisition of Essar Steel, once controlled by former billionaires Shashi and Ravi Ruia.
Mittal has held a board seat at Goldman Sachs since 2008.
Mittal has received the Padma Vibhushan, India's second highest civilian honour, and a Forbes Lifetime Achievement Award.

name: Karl Albrecht Jr.
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Karl Albrecht Jr. is the son of Karl Albrecht Sr., the late grocery billionaire who died in 2014 at age 94. He and his sister, Beate Heister, are billionaire heirs to the Aldi retail fortune.
After World War II, Karl Sr. and his brother, Theo Sr., who died in 2010 at age 88, took over their family's corner grocery store in Essen, Germany.
In 1961, the brothers split ownership: Karl Sr. took the stores in southern Germany (Aldi Sued), plus rights to the Aldi brand in the U.K., Australia and the U.S.
In the U.S., Aldi has more than 2,000 stores in 36 states, offering low prices and no-frills shopping.
Theo Sr. got the stores in northern Germany and the rest of Europe. In 1971, he bought U.S. grocery chain Trader Joe's.
forbes_facts: Karl Jr., who has no children, worked different positions at the company but withdrew from his duties after a cancer diagnosis.

name: Zhou Qunfei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2017-2025); Wikidata (2016)
forbes_bio: Zhou Qunfei is the chairman and general manager of Lens Technology, a touch screen maker whose customers include Apple, Samsung and Huawei.
It also supplies to electric vehicle makers such as Tesla and BYD.
A migrant factory worker as a teenager, Zhou has gone on to become one of the world's richest self-made women.
Lens Technology went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2015, 22 years after she founded the company. It had a dual listing in Hong Kong in July 2025.
Zhou first took the plunge as an entrepreneur in 1993 when she set up a watch parts company, the precursor of Lens, with relatives in an apartment in Shenzhen.
forbes_facts: Growing up she helped her family raise pigs and ducks for food and additional money.
Zhou dropped out of school at 16 and traveled south to Guangdong province to live with her uncle's family and search for better work.

name: Wang Laichun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2017-2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Laichun, also known as Grace Wang, is the chairman and general manager of electronics component manufacturer Luxshare Precision Industry.
One of the company's most important customers is Apple. CEO Tim Cook has visited its China factories often.
Wang worked for Taiwanese billionaire Terry Gou's Hon Hai Precision Industry (also known as Foxconn) for 10 years.
Wang left in 1997 and teamed up with her brother Wang Laisheng to set up Luxshare in 2004; he is now the vice chairman.
Luxshare went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2010. It had a dual listing in Hong Kong in July 2026.

Hong-tu's son, Tzung-han, was appointed vice chairman of Cathay in 2025.

name: Michael Otto
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Michael Otto inherited shares in the retail empire his late father, Werner Otto, founded as a mail-order business in Hamburg in 1949.
As chief executive, he ran his family's Otto Group for 26 years until 2007. He is now chairman of its supervisory board.
With revenues exceeding $15 billion, Otto Group has more than 40 companies in retail (including Crate and Barrel), real estate and financial services.
Michael's stepmother Maren and her children Alexander and Katharina -- all billionaires -- also own stakes in Otto Group.
Separate from Michael, they own ECE Group, a real estate company focused on shopping centers, and a stake in office property firm Paramount Group.
forbes_facts: Michael's son, Benjamin, announced he wouldn't be following his dad's footsteps and become chief executive. He is managing partner instead.
Michael's half-sister, Katharina Otto-Bernstein, writes and produces art movies in the U.S.

name: Arturo Moreno
sec_insider_companies: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. (CCO) - TenPercentOwner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: Arturo Moreno is the owner of the Los Angeles Angels baseball team, which he bought in 2003 for $184 million. It is now worth about $2.75 billion.
Moreno's initial fortune came from billboard advertising company Outdoor Systems, which he sold to Infinity Broadcasting in 1999 for $8.3 billion.
He has stakes in other billboard advertising companies, as well as commercial real estate holdings throughout Phoenix.
Moreno's $325 million plan to develop a new Angels baseball stadium was scuttled in 2022, by Anaheim's City Council.
A few months later, Moreno announced he intended to sell the Angels to the highest bidder but later changed his mind.
forbes_facts: The oldest of 11 children, Moreno was drafted into the Vietnam War before attending the University of Arizona on the G.I. Bill.
When Moreno bought the Angels, he became the first Mexican-American to own a major league sports team.
